teams.heading: Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada rates Fiji's physicality impressive ahead of Twickenham rematch
teams.body: Quesada told his pre-match press conference that playing the same side twice helps preparation, though he reminded listeners rugby is not purely physical. The Italian federation's own review of Fiji's 21-16 win in Udine last weekend credits the visitors with slowing Azzurri rucks and winning several turnovers at the breakdown. Jake White has since made nine changes for today's 11th-place final at Twickenham. He starts Tamani and Muntz at half-back and hands the front row to Ravuiwasa, Narisia and Nairau.

lead.why: Newest Fiji-centred item: the opposing coach's verdict on Fiji's physicality before the rematch. Candidate 3 is likely rugby league and was set aside.

teams.heading: Former England scrum-half and Rugby Special presenter Nigel Starmer-Smith dies aged 81
teams.body: His family announced the death on Thursday. A Harlequins and Barbarians scrum-half, Starmer-Smith made seven appearances for England between 1969 and 1971 before moving into the media, where he fronted the BBC's weekly highlights programme Rugby Special for 15 years. He had been diagnosed with dementia in 2015. His son Charlie called him "one of life's great tourists" — a player, commentator, editor, writer and charity fundraiser who would "hate for people to make a fuss."

lead.why: The death of a former England international is a genuinely new event, while the Fisilau selection is part of the team announcement already covered on Thursday.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos set to return at fullback for France against Springboks
teams.body: Rugbyrama reports that Ramos will start at No. 15 in Sunday's Nations Championship final against the Springboks at Twickenham, with the official team due on Friday. Toulouse's goal-kicker has not played since 27 September. A thigh injury and then a relapse cost him France's three earlier November tests, including the 21-19 win over South Africa. Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang's ankle sprain, picked up against Argentina, and Romain Ntamack's unavailability shaped the call: Théo Attissogbe moves to the wing to make room.

lead.why: A fresh selection event: France's first-choice goal-kicker returns from injury to start the final.

teams.heading: Farrell hands Sam Prendergast fourth November start at No. 10 against Australia
teams.body: Prendergast has started all three November games, and Farrell resisted the case for Ciarán Frawley, again on the bench, saying the 23-year-old Leinster man has "got his mojo back and is playing some excellent rugby," and wants to see him back it up. The shirt opened up with Jack Crowley sidelined: the Munster out-half remains out with a vascular issue in his leg but was in camp before the Springbok win and has begun a gradual return that Farrell insists will not be rushed.

lead.why: Farrell's fly-half call for Australia, with Crowley's recovery update, is fresh senior selection news about Ireland.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada calls out Italy's attitude against South Africa, Australia and Wales
teams.body: Against the Springboks, the Italy coach said, his side did not even believe they could compete. He also singled out the Australia match and passages against Wales as moments when Italy were not themselves. Speaking before the 11th-place final against Fiji at Twickenham, Quesada said he was dissatisfied with results but calm and clear-headed: the defeats to Argentina and Fiji showed Italy can build the conditions to win, only to fall short of finishing the job. What is missing, he added, is a little confidence.

lead.why: Quesada's frank review of where Italy's attitude failed is the freshest Italy story not already covered by this week's selection and captaincy editions.

teams.heading: Scotland take on Argentina at Twickenham after trading wins over past year
teams.body: Sunday's Twickenham warm-up act to the France–South Africa grand final pits fourth from the northern hemisphere against fourth from the south. Gregor Townsend's side lost at home to the Pumas last November before winning in Argentina in July. Scotland arrive off an 11-try, 67-5 rout of Japan, though BBC Scotland's Tom English singled out the seven penalties they conceded in that game's first half as the soft moments stronger opponents punish.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy restores James Botham and hands Dafydd Jenkins captaincy for Japan
teams.body: Tandy has made five changes, four of them in the pack, for Saturday's ninth-place final. Botham was player of the match in Wales's 35-28 win over New Zealand but was a surprise omission from the matchday 23 for the 29-26 defeat by Australia. He now joins Alex Mann and Aaron Wainwright. Jenkins takes the armband from Dewi Lake, who drops to the bench with Jac Morgan as Ryan Elias starts at hooker. Rhys Carre and Adam Beard also come in. "We were always looking to rotate and rest up a few boys," Tandy explained.

lead.why: The confirmed Wales XV is the day's fresh event, and Botham's recall and the new captain are the angles the reader has not yet seen.

teams.heading: Contepomi adds six to Pumas squad, Moroni one cap from centurion status
teams.body: Bautista Delguy (knee), Mateo Carreras (shoulder), Santiago Chocobares and Pablo Matera, out for personal reasons, all miss the seventh-place final against Scotland, with Mayco Vivas gone after his red card in Paris. In come hooker Ignacio Ruiz, flanker Santiago Grondona, loose head Rodrigo Martínez, wing Santiago Pernas, uncapped fly-half Juan Segundo Martín Montilla and centre Matías Moroni. Should the veteran of three World Cups feature, he would become the second Pumas back to reach 100 tests, after Nicolás Sánchez.

lead.why: Contepomi's six call-ups, including a possible 100th cap for Moroni, are the freshest Pumas story not yet run.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell names full-strength Ireland side to face Les Kiss's Wallabies
teams.body: Ireland were widely expected to rotate for the fifth-place final. Instead, Farrell has kept the side that beat the Springboks 20-17 and changed only what he had to. Nick Timoney replaces the suspended Dan Sheehan at No. 8, Tadhg Beirne takes the captaincy and Jacob Stockdale comes in for Mack Hansen. The42 reads it as respect for Kiss's side. It recalls July's 33-31 Ireland win in Sydney, when Ben Donaldson missed a kick at goal with the last play of the game.

lead.why: Fresh selection story that sets the strength of the side the Wallabies face in their season finale.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones hands Taufa Latu first Test start in wholesale Japan changes
teams.body: Latu, who came off the bench last week, is promoted for Saturday's ninth-place final against Wales, with Michael Stolberg partnering captain Warner Dearns in the second row. Jones keeps the same back row, including Ben Gunter, who leads the competition with 11 dominant tackles and six jackals. Co-captain Naoto Saito starts at scrum-half. Ryosuke Iwaihara and Seina Kimura were ruled out after the 67-5 defeat by Scotland.

teams.heading: Stade Français land All Blacks loose forward Wallace Sititi from the Chiefs
teams.body: The Top 14 club have secured the Chiefs back-rower for the 2027/28 season, on reports, and are looking to make further serious moves in the market. L'Équipe reports the Parisians are in advanced talks with double World Cup-winning Springbok lock RG Snyman, contracted to Leinster until the end of 2026/27. Sititi is not the only All Black bound for Europe — Planet Rugby reports Beauden Barrett has signed a two-year deal with Bristol Bears.

teams.heading: Siya Kolisi says Springboks want to win final for banned Rassie Erasmus
teams.body: Speaking at Twickenham on Wednesday, the captain stressed that Erasmus still coaches the squad all week and is barred only on match day. Erasmus is serving a six-game suspension for suggesting officiating in the 21-19 defeat by France in Paris amounted to "match-fixing". Kolisi called that absence tough before the Nations Championship final against Les Bleus, adding: "we'd love to do it for him." The Boks will also be without injured flank Pieter-Steph du Toit, whom he called "a big loss."

lead.why: The captain's first word on playing the final for a banned coach, plus confirmation that Pieter-Steph du Toit is out, is the freshest Springbok story; the World Rugby investigation already ran yesterd
